requirements.businessContext: People sign in with Google, pick one unique username, and join any number of members-mode leagues through invite links; TVT/Continental teammates each have their own account. The session identifies the person; the league comes from the URL and team_members decides the team on every request. Legacy leagues (a team ID and password per team) keep working unchanged until the end of the 2026-27 season. Design: docs/10-accounts-and-membership.md.

userStories.iWant: to sign in with my Google account and pick one username
userStories.soThat: I don't juggle a login per team or league

userStories.iWant: to join a league from an invite link
userStories.soThat: my league admin doesn't have to hand out credentials

userStories.iWant: to invite my teammate with a link
userStories.soThat: they play on our team with their own sign-in

userStories.iWant: to switch between my leagues without signing in again
userStories.soThat: managing all my teams is quick

userStories.iWant: to share one link, approve joins if I choose, and assign or remove people by username
to sign out of all other devices or delete my account
userStories.soThat: I stay in control of my access and data

userStories.iWant: to move a person's teams to a new account
userStories.soThat: a lost Google account doesn't lose their teams

userStories.iWant: to create admins by email and have removal take effect immediately
userStories.soThat: admin access is easy to grant and safe to revoke

businessRules.rule: A person is on at most one team per league (unique league_id + user_id); a team has at most one owner.

Team-scoped APIs resolve the team via resolveTeamActor: a legacy login is its own team; a person is their membership in the league named by ?league= (or the team named). Never from the session id directly.
Removing a member, replacing an account or bumping users.session_version takes effect on the next request.
League invites default to 14 days and one use per team; partner invites are single-use for 7 days; regenerating revokes the previous link.
Password sign-in is refused for Google-only accounts and for team keys of members-mode leagues.
In-app browsers (WhatsApp, Instagram, ...) get an open-in-browser screen instead of the Google button.
Post-sign-in redirects only ever go to same-site paths.
The repo talks only to a local file: database or the jpl-india Turso database.
Members-mode backups leave Password blank and list members; restore preserves memberships.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a new person signed in with Google
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are sent to onboarding before joining anything

acceptanceCriteria.given: a valid league invite and a signed-in person with a username
acceptanceCriteria.then: they own the first open team and land on that league's setup
they join the same team as member, and the link can't be reused

acceptanceCriteria.given: a person on teams in two leagues
acceptanceCriteria.then: each action lands on that league's team

acceptanceCriteria.given: a person not on a team in a league
acceptanceCriteria.when: they call that league's team or auction APIs

acceptanceCriteria.then: a request waits until an admin approves (team claimed) or rejects

acceptanceCriteria.given: an expired, revoked or used-up invite, or a full league
acceptanceCriteria.then: they get a clear message and no team

acceptanceCriteria.when: one chooses sign out of all other devices
acceptanceCriteria.then: the other is signed out on its next request

acceptanceCriteria.given: an admin removed by the superadmin
acceptanceCriteria.when: they make their next admin request

acceptanceCriteria.given: a person's seat moved to a new account
acceptanceCriteria.when: the old account makes its next request
acceptanceCriteria.then: it no longer reaches the team

acceptanceCriteria.when: the sign-in or join page opens
acceptanceCriteria.then: an open-in-browser screen replaces the Google button

acceptanceCriteria.when: it is backed up and restored
